info.title: Nova API
info.description: The stardelt Nova gateway: catalog browse, queries and jobs over one identity. In `dev` mode (the default) every route answers without sign-in; in `oidc` mode every described route below requires a session or bearer token except this document itself. Only routes tagged `public` are promised stable. Every non-2xx answer is `{"error": "<one sentence>"}` (`ErrorResponse`), unless the operation documents another body: `POST /api/migrations/apply` answers 409 with `ApplyAnswer` and the refused migration file. A missing or invalid credential is 401 with an `ErrorResponse` on every operation the global `security` covers; the three routes that answer without a credential (the document itself, health and the sign-in config) carry an empty `security`.

servers.description: This Nova instance. Every path below starts with `/api`; a missing or invalid credential is answered with 401 and an ErrorResponse.

get.description: Every `Catalog` of the platform namespace, ordered bronze, silver, gold, then the rest alphabetically (`layer`: the `stardelt.io/layer` label, else the catalog's own name; `environment`: `production` when the resource carries `stardelt.io/environment: production`, absent otherwise): identity, owner, managed access, the storage key prefix, phase and the grants and conditions the access-sync job last wrote. Administrator-only; a non-administrator answers 403 `this view is for platform administrators`. The write is `PUT /api/admin/catalogs/{name}/access`; this route never changes anything. A catalog the job has not observed yet answers `phase: "Unknown"` with no conditions. Without a cluster connection (demo mode, a local run) the answer is the one in-memory `warehouse` catalog. Answers `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: One row per catalog, medallion layers first, then by name

403.description: The caller is not a platform administrator

502.description: The cluster did not answer, or Nova may not list catalogs

put.description: Change one catalog's `spec.owner`, `spec.managedAccess` and `spec.grants` as a JSON merge patch on the `Catalog` resource, carrying the `resourceVersion` the page read. Administrator-only; a non-administrator answers 403 `this view is for platform administrators`. A malformed owner, group name, verb or a duplicate grant is a 400 in the words the form shows; a catalog that changed meanwhile is a 409 `this catalog changed since you opened it; reload`, and a catalog a GitOps tool owns (Argo CD or Flux, from its annotations or labels) is a 409 `<name> is managed by <tool>: change its grants in Git` with nothing patched; a name that is not a catalog or no longer exists is a 404; more than 30 changes per administrator in an hour is a 429. Without a cluster connection the answer is 503 `the cluster is not reachable from Nova` (demo mode changes memory instead). Answers the updated row, the same shape as the list, with the new `metadata.generation`; `status.observedGeneration` catches up when the access-sync job runs (about two minutes). Never carries a storage credential. `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.description: Create a new team space in one call: the `Catalog` resources `<team>` (production), `<team>lab` (the team's sandbox) and `<team>ref` (shared reference data), each owned by `group` with the four verbs `browse`, `select`, `write` and `create` for `group` and for `stardelt-admins`, plus the `ServicePrincipal` `pipeline-<group>` when it does not exist yet (it may already serve another team of the same group). The group must already exist in the company's sign-in provider — stardelt never creates groups. Administrator-only; a non-administrator answers 403 `this view is for platform administrators`. A team name outside 2 to 21 lower-case letters and digits starting with a letter, a group name outside the group rule, or a description over 500 characters is a 400; any of the three catalogs already existing is a 409 `the catalog <name> already exists` with nothing created, and a platform without any `Catalog` is a 409 `no lakehouse to put the catalogs in`; more than ten team spaces per administrator in an hour is a 429. When the API server refuses one of the creates the answer is a 502 naming what failed and what was created so far; nothing is rolled back, so a half-created space stays visible and can be finished by hand. Without a cluster connection the answer is 503 `the cluster is not reachable from Nova`. Answers 201 with the three catalog names and the principal, `Cache-Control: no-store`.

post.summary: `POST /api/ask` — a question in, checked SQL out.
post.description: A question in words, one Trino statement out. Nova searches the catalog as the caller for at most five tables, sends the question and **the documentation of those tables only** — description, tags, owner, domain, column names and their descriptions — to the first `ModelEndpoint` (name order) whose purpose list contains `ask` and whose probe found it reachable with JSON output, and answers the statement the model writes. No row, no query result and no table data ever leaves the platform, whatever the endpoint's `sendRows` says; never the endpoint's URL or its key either. The statement is **checked with `EXPLAIN` as the caller and is not run**: `explain` is `passed` or `failed`, and a failed check keeps the SQL in the answer with the engine's sentence in `error` (one correction is asked of the model first). No matching table is a `200` with `sql: null` and a sentence saying so; a model endpoint that is refused, unreachable or does not answer in the JSON shape is a `502`. A spent budget is the `429` the model budget answers (see `/api/admin/model-usage`). Every answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.

200.description: The statement, its sentence, the tables it was written for and the `EXPLAIN` result

400.description: The question is empty or longer than 2000 characters

401.description: Not signed in

429.description: The person's or their group's model budget is spent

502.description: The catalog, the cluster or the model endpoint did not answer

503.description: No state store, no cluster connection, no HTTP client, or no ready `ask` endpoint

post.summary: `POST /api/ask/feedback` — one 👍 or 👎 on the row an Ask answer wrote (nova#891 slice b).
post.description: Writes the caller's own 👍 or 👎 on the `model_call` row that `/api/ask` returned as `callId` — the row the answer's model call wrote, and the input of the model check. A vote is `up` or `down`. A call id that belongs to somebody else is a `404`, never a `403`: an id probe learns nothing. The vote overwrites the row's earlier one; retention is the row's own. Every answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.

get.description: The catalogs the caller may browse, each with its Lakekeeper warehouse id and its medallion layer when it has one, plus the catalog a request without `?catalog=` uses. Its `owner` is `spec.owner` of the catalog's `Catalog` resource and `description` is `spec.description` (null without a resource); `grants` is `spec.grants` in declared order — one group and one verb (`browse`, `select`, `write`, `create`, `manage`) each — and empty when the catalog declares none, so a member can see whose data it is and which groups may read or write it. The order is bronze, silver, gold first (in that order), then the rest alphabetically; `layer` is `stardelt.io/layer` from the catalog's `Catalog` resource, else the catalog's own name when that is `bronze`, `silver` or `gold`, and absent otherwise; `environment` is `production` when the resource carries `stardelt.io/environment: production`, and absent otherwise. The list is what the engine's `SHOW CATALOGS` shows the caller (through the caller's own token), minus the engine's own catalogs (`system`, `information_schema`, `memory`, `tpch`, `tpcds`, `jmx`); it is cached for 30 s (the layer for 60 s; the owner and grants are read on every request). Every other `/api/catalog/*` route takes the same `?catalog=`; a catalog the caller may not browse answers 403 there and is never proxied. Empty when no catalog is open to the caller. `demo` in demo mode.

200.description: The browsable catalogs and the default one

502.description: The query engine or the catalog is not reachable

503.description: A catalog the engine lists has no warehouse

get.description: What is in each catalog the caller may browse: schemas, tables, rows, bytes on the object store and the newest commit, plus the sums. Rows are ordered bronze, silver, gold first, then by name, and carry `layer` when the catalog is one of the three (the `stardelt.io/layer` label, else the catalog's own name). The catalog list is the caller's own `SHOW CATALOGS` (`GET /api/catalog/catalogs`); a catalog the caller may not browse is never read and never appears. The numbers come from the catalog's Iceberg metadata (the current snapshot's `total-records` and `total-files-size`), so the endpoint runs no query, and they are read in the background every five minutes (`NOVA_METRICS_REFRESH_SECS`): a request answers from the last numbers at once, whatever their age, and `updatedAt` says when they were read. A catalog with no numbers yet is answered with zeros and `pending: true` while one background scan reads it; `totals` leave pending rows out. At most 200 tables per catalog are loaded: `truncated` says the rows and bytes are a sample while `tables` stays exact. A catalog whose scan failed keeps its last numbers and carries an `error` sentence (zeros for one that never answered); only an unreachable engine or catalog fails the request with 502. 403 when no catalog is open to the caller. Never cached by the client.

200.description: One entry per browsable catalog, medallion layers first, then by name, with the totals

403.description: No catalog is open to the caller

502.description: The query engine is not reachable, so the catalogs cannot be named

post.description: Read every catalog again now, instead of waiting for the next background round (every five minutes). Administrator only: it is an operator action on the whole warehouse, and `main` puts the same `require_admin` in front of it as `/api/apps`, so a non-administrator answers 403. Answers 202 — the round runs in the background, one at a time, and the page reads the new numbers with its next `GET /api/catalog/metrics`. At most one per minute: a second call answers 429 with the sentence `the numbers were refreshed less than a minute ago`.

put.description: Set or remove a table's description, tags, owner, domain and guide in one Lakekeeper commit. `?catalog=` picks the catalog. Every key is optional: absent changes nothing, `null` (or an empty tag list, or a blank description or guide) removes the property, and a write with nothing to change sends no commit. Description at most 4,000 characters; guide at most 16,000 characters and keeps its line breaks; at most 20 unique tags `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$`; owner a group name; domain `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,39}$`. An ownerless table may be edited by anybody, but the request must then set `owner` to one of the caller's own groups. **The interim rule is enforced by Nova; the catalog does not enforce it yet** — anyone who reaches Lakekeeper or Trino directly can still change these properties. Edits of one table are serialised by Nova and a contended commit is retried; a catalog that stays busy answers 502 `the catalog is busy, try again`. Demo mode answers 503.

get.summary: `GET /api/compute`: the Spark clusters this caller may use.
get.description: The Spark clusters the caller may use: an administrator sees every `SparkCluster` of the platform namespace, everyone else the ones owned by one of their groups, owned by them (`owner.user` is the sign-in name) and the `shared` one. Each row carries the owner, the class `size`, the `runtime`, the operator's `phase` (`Starting` for a requested `Running` before it has reported, `Stopped` otherwise) and `message`, the operator's reason while a cluster is `Failed` (a refused `SparkConnect`, a runtime that is not in the catalogue, a driver that cannot start), the Connect `endpoint` and `startedAt` while it runs (`endpoint` is absent when the caller reaches the cluster only through `spec.viewers`: such a server acts with its owner group's rights, so Nova issues a viewer no channel — #493), `lastActivityAt` once the operator reports it, `idleStopMinutes` (`0` on the shared cluster), `canUse`, `canAct`, whether the caller may start, stop or edit the cluster, and `shared`. post.description: Say what applying one bundle's rendered Pipeline documents to one stage would do, writing nothing. Every document goes through the same create rules `pipelines_validate` and the write routes use, so the plan and the apply cannot disagree: `changes` names a `create`, an `update` (with the sentences it would change) or an `unchanged` document, `errors` carries the rule that refuses one, and `warnings` names a pipeline this bundle and stage own that the set does not name (a warning unless `prune` is true, when it is a `delete` change). `files` says which of the bundle's files are new against the newest applied deployment of this bundle and stage. `planId` is the identity of the rendered set: the SHA-256 of the bundle, the stage, the documents in the order given and the files sorted by path. A later `POST /api/deployments` may carry it as `planId`, and answers 409 when the row's set is not the planned one. A `prune: true` request names each owned pipeline the set omits as a `delete` change. The stage modes are not covered yet; a StreamApp document is checked with the rules its write runs, and every stream change reads as a create because a stream write is a PUT. A token issued to the Keycloak client `stardelt-deploy-<stage>` (a deploy principal, #57) answers 403 unless the target is `<stage>` and the caller is a member of the owner group; an administrator's credential has no such client and is unaffected.

put.summary: `PUT /api/notebooks/{group}/{name}`: validate, strip, store one immutable version.
put.description: Publish a notebook as a new immutable object version in the `notebooks` bucket. Needs a signed-in person whose groups include `{group}` (403 `you are not a member of the group <g>`; administrators are not exempt). `{name}` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._ -]{0,127}\.ipynb$` and the body must be an nbformat 4 notebook of at most 5 MiB. Every code cell's `outputs` is emptied and its `execution_count` set to null, and the notebook's widget metadata is removed, before storing — no cell output reaches the object store. A cell of an nbformat 4.5 notebook without an `id` gets one (`cell-<position>`), so the stored notebook stays valid nbformat. `sha256` is of the stored (stripped) bytes. `parameters` are the `name = literal` lines of the first cell tagged `parameters`, at most 32; defaults are text and are never evaluated. A 61st publish by one person in an hour is 429. Publishing bytes the newest version already holds stores nothing, uses no slot and writes no audit line: the answer names that version with `unchanged: true`. With `?dryRun=true` the same checks run and nothing is stored, no slot is used and no audit line is written: the answer says `unchanged: true` with the newest version, or `unchanged: false` with an empty `objectVersion` when a publish would store a new one. Unset `NOVA_S3_*` is 503 `notebook storage is not configured`; an S3 that is down or refuses is 502. Each publish that stores a version writes one audit line with group, name, version and size, never content. A version published with an `X-Stardelt-Source` header carries `source` (`repository`, `commit`, `path`, `clean`); Nova stores it and does not verify it against a Git server. A version published with an `X-Stardelt-Viewers` header carries up to 8 group names that may read it without being members; the JSON is stored with the version.

when there is no resource or it names no owner (stardelt-nova#577).

CatalogMaintenance.description: What the newest finished `maint-<catalog>` Job did (operator#476 slice c).

error.description:
Why this catalog could not be read — absent for a catalog that was. A sentence,
never URL, token or stack trace.

pending.description:
No numbers yet — the catalog appeared after the last round (or before the first),
and one scan is reading it now. Its numbers are zeros and the totals leave it out.

updatedAt.description:
When these numbers were read (Unix ms), so the page can say "Updated 4 minutes
ago". `null` while `pending`: there are no numbers yet.

CatalogMetricsView.description:
One catalog in the answer: the numbers, plus the sentence when the last scan failed. A
failed catalog is zeros only when it never answered — a catalog that answered once
keeps those numbers — never omitted: a page that silently drops a catalog says "you
have none", which is not what happened.

CatalogStats.description: One catalog's numbers, as the endpoint answers them.

lastCommitMs.description: The newest commit among the loaded tables (Unix ms); `null` when none has one.

layer.description:
`bronze`, `silver` or `gold` when the catalog is a medallion layer (see
`crate::catalog::catalog_layers`); absent for every other catalog.

name.description: Catalog name, as the engine and the catalog spell it.

records.description: Rows in the loaded tables' current snapshots.

sizeBytes.description: Bytes the loaded tables' current snapshots occupy on the object store.

tables.description: Tables in the catalog — every one the catalog lists, loaded or not.

truncated.description:
More tables exist than the endpoint loads (200 per catalog): `tables` is exact,
`records` and `sizeBytes` cover the first 200 only.

CatalogsResponse.description:
`GET /api/catalog/catalogs`: the catalogs the caller may browse, the medallion layers
first.

catalogs.description:
Every catalog the caller may browse (`?catalog=` accepts any of these names),
ordered bronze, silver, gold, then the rest alphabetically.

default.description: The catalog a request without `?catalog=` works in.

CheckAllAnswer.description:
`POST /api/catalog/tables/{ns}/{tbl}/verified-queries/check` answer: every query of one
table checked, with the totals.

items.description: The rows as the checks left them, in id order.

CheckStatementRequest.description: `POST /api/pipelines/check`: what the engine says about a statement, without running it.

params.description: The parameters the statement's `${params.<name>}` placeholders are filled with.

CheckStatementResponse.description:
The engine's verdict. `checked: false` means this kind of statement cannot be checked here;
`ok` is absent then.

message.description: The engine's sentence when `ok` is false.

CheckView.description:
One check of one `quality` task. `rows` and `passed` are `None` until the task's log
carries the line (the task has not run, or has not reached the check yet).

name.description: The check's name, as declared in `spec.tasks[].checks[].name`.

passed.description: `Some(rows == 0)` once the log carries the line, `None` before that.

rows.description: The rows the assertion returned; `0` is a pass.

ChecksResponse.description: `GET …/runs/{run_id}/checks`: one row per declared check of the run's `quality` tasks.

rows.description: One array per row, in column order.

type.description: The engine's type name, for example `varchar` or `bigint`.

ColumnDocumentation.description: One column of the current schema, as the documentation read reports it.

name.description: Field name, exactly as the current schema spells it.

type.description: The field's type as text; a complex type is its JSON text.

ColumnSource.description:
One source column of an output column. A source outside the caller's catalogs is
answered as `{ "hidden": true }`, without names.

ComputeCluster.description: One `SparkCluster`, as the Compute page needs it.

audience.description: `members` or `visitors`: who shares a platform server.

canAct.description:
Whether the caller may start, stop or edit the cluster: an administrator, the owner
group of a `SparkCluster`, its `owner.user`, or an administrator on `shared` (#706).

kind.description: `cluster` for a `SparkCluster`, `platform` for a Spark server the manifests install.

oneOf.description: The container's resource limits, on a platform server.

message.description:
The operator's reason while the phase is `Failed` or `Starting` (for example a refused
`SparkConnect`, a runtime that is not in the catalogue, or a driver that cannot start).

mode.description: `kubernetes` (executors are pods) or `local` (the demo sandbox: two threads, none).

resetsAt.description: When a platform server is restarted on a schedule (`daily 03:00 UTC` on the sandbox).

viewers.description: The groups that may see the cluster without being its owner (`spec.viewers`).

yours.description: Whether this is the Spark the caller's own notebook uses.

ComputeEnvVar.description:
One environment variable of the driver and executors. `value` only: the operator
refuses `connectionRef` until internal#161 slice 7, so Nova does not offer it.

ComputeOwner.description: The `SparkCluster`'s owner: a group or a person, exactly one of the two.

ComputeResources.description: The pod shape of a driver or executor (`spec.driver` / `spec.executor`).

ComputeSpecBody.description:
The body of `PUT /api/admin/compute/{name}`: everything an administrator may set.
No `state` — Start and Stop own it — and no `metadata`.

viewers.description:
Groups that may see the cluster without being its owner (`spec.viewers`), read-only.
Absent keeps what the cluster carries; an empty list removes the key. At most 16.

ConnectionView.description: One row of `GET /api/connections`. Never carries a value.

oneOf.description: The last break-glass read of a group connection; absent for personal and managed rows.

member.description:
Whether the caller belongs to the scope that owns this row: `true` for a personal or managed
connection and for a group connection of one of the caller's groups; `false` for a group
connection an administrator sees only because they are an administrator. `false` means
read-only for this person — no create, no rotation — except delete and break-glass.

secretKeys.description: The names of the secret fields.

oneOf.description: `Ready` and its reason from the resource's status; absent for a personal connection.

namespace.description: Schema name to create (surrounding whitespace is trimmed).

CreatePipelineRequest.description: `POST /api/pipelines`: schedule a statement for one of the caller's own groups.

oneOf.description: A published notebook version to run instead of a statement (#237).

Who is told when a run ends (`spec.notify`). Omitted writes none; every name must be a
destination of `ownerGroup`.

Retries, the wait between them, the time limit and the run mode; omitted fields keep the
defaults.

params.description:
Values for `${params.<name>}` in the statement; at most 16. A notebook's values are in
`notebook.params`, not here.

oneOf.description: Which bundle, target and commit this pipeline is deployed from (`stardelt bundle deploy`).

How the writes reach the tables people read (`spec.publish`, #114). Omitted on a create
means `direct`; on an update it keeps what the pipeline says, and `direct` removes it.

sql.description: The statement to run; exactly one of this and `notebook` is given.

tasks.description:
A whole task list instead of one `run` task (`#905`): 1 to 30 tasks, each a statement, a
pinned notebook, a dbt run or SQL checks, with dependencies. Exclusive with `sql` and
`notebook`.

viewers.description:
Groups that may read the pipeline without being members (`spec.viewers`). At most 16,
each a group name; omitted writes none. A bundle's pipeline file carries it (#79).

DbStatus.description: What `/api/health` reports about the state store.

DbtRequest.description:
A `dbt` task of a task list (`#112`): a project of the tool image, one selector or a chain
of batches, the threads and the `--vars` text. The rules are `demos/dags/stardelt_pipelines/
plan.py`'s, so Nova refuses what the loader would refuse.

batches.description: 1 to 8 selectors, run in order (`config.batches` as the JSON array text).

project.description: A directory name under `/opt/dbt/projects` in the tool image.

deletedVersions.description: How many object versions were removed.

Deployment.description: A row as the API returns it. `created_at` is RFC 3339 in UTC.

actor.description: The `sub` of the person who recorded the deploy.

actorName.description: The name the caller's sign-in provided; `None` for rows recorded before migration 0025.

files.description: The files of the bundle the deploy read, as the caller sent them.

pipelines.description: The pipelines the deploy touched, as the caller sent them.

previousDeploymentId.description: The deployment this row replayed, when it is a rollback; `None` for a deploy that was not one.

resources.description: The rendered Pipeline documents the deploy applied, as the caller sent them.

DeploymentFile.description: One file of the bundle the deploy read: its path inside the bundle and the sha256 of its bytes.

path.description: The path relative to the bundle directory, with `/` separators.

sha256.description: The file's content, lowercase hex sha256 (64 characters).

DeploymentPipeline.description: One pipeline of a deploy: what changed in it.

DeploymentView.description: What `view_of` shows of a [`Provenance`], with who deployed and when.

modified.description:
`true` when what the deploy decides differs from what it wrote: a pipeline's run,
schedule, parameters and options, or a stream's source, sink, engine and restart policy.
Someone used the form, the YAML editor or `kubectl` since. Left out when they match, and
for a resource stamped before the digest existed.

repository.description: The repository the bundle was read from: `https://host/path`, for the compare link.

Destination.description: A named email or webhook endpoint owned by one group (`GET /api/destinations`).

viewers.description: Groups that may see this destination, read-only. Empty: its owner group only.

detail.description: One sentence; never the URL or a header value.

status.description: The webhook's HTTP status, when it answered.

DocumentationUpdate.description:
`PUT /api/catalog/tables/{ns}/{tbl}/documentation` body.

Every key is optional. Absent changes nothing; `null` removes the property; an empty tag
list and a blank description also remove. A field whose value equals what the table
already stores is not a change.

guide.description: New guide (`null` or blank removes it).

tags.description: New tag list (`null` or `[]` removes them).

Embed.description: Whether Nova can frame an app, as observed from the app's own headers.

blocked_by.description: The header that refuses framing, e.g. `content-security-policy`.

checked.description: The in-cluster page Nova read the headers from.

detail.description: That header's value, verbatim — what the operator has to change.

sign_in_host.description:
Host a visitor without a session is sent to for sign-in, when the app's
own page redirects off its hosts before it renders. That page (Keycloak
on this platform) refuses framing, so the frame stays empty until the
visitor signs in in a top-level tab; the UI turns this into a call to
action. `None` when the app answers for itself — a login form on its own
host is part of the app and frames fine.

url.description: The page a browser loads in the frame (external URL, empty without a base domain).

EmbedApp.description:
What the embedded pages (Dashboards, Notebooks) need, readable by every signed-in user:
the apps Nova frames, their address, liveness and framing state. No workloads, images or
replica counts; those stay behind the admin-only `/api/apps`.

Deliberately not an admin route and deliberately not a filtered `/api/apps`: an ordinary
user needs to open the notebook and the dashboard, and nothing else on that payload.

ErrorResponse.description:
Every non-2xx answer under `/api/` is this envelope (see README "HTTP
conventions"), so every error response in the document points here.

error.description: Human-readable sentence. Never contains tokens, URLs or stack traces.

Fact.description: One label/value pair about an app, as Nova can honestly observe it.

source.description:
Where the value comes from, e.g. `Trino /v1/info`. Facts without a source
are those Nova knows from its own configuration.

tone.description: `ok` | `bad` when the value is a health judgement; absent otherwise.

HistoryRun.description: One earlier run of the same statement (nova#788 S4).

endedAt.description: Finished at, epoch milliseconds; null while the engine never reported an end.

runs.description: The runs of this job that wrote this edge in the window.

LineageImpact.description:
The whole closure, at any number of steps (nova#646 L8a). The drawn graph keeps `depth`;
these numbers answer "what breaks if I change this table".

downstream.description: Distinct visible datasets reachable downstream at any number of steps; the focus is not one.

downstreamJobs.description: Distinct jobs (`(job_ns, job)`) on the downstream flows.

LineageJob.description: One job that wrote an edge of the answer, with its runs in the window.

handMade.description: True when every used flow that touches this node was a hand-made (ad-hoc) job.

lastWrite.description: The newest event time of an edge that wrote this node.

level.description: 0 for the focus table, negative upstream, positive downstream (visible nodes only).

oneOf.description: Read-only queries against this node in the window (visible nodes only).

writers.description: The jobs that wrote this node, newest first; only on the focus node.

people.description: Distinct people: the SQL editor and notebooks, never a BI tool.

tools.description: The tools that read this node, most queries first, at most 5.

LineageWriter.description: One job that wrote the focus table, with its runs in the window.

Link.description: A deep link into an app's own UI.

LogLine.description: One log message. `sources` is deliberately absent: it names internal object-store paths.

LogView.description: One page of a task's log.

McpCall.description: One recorded call. `atMs` is epoch milliseconds, like every other time in Nova's API.

McpCalls.description: The answer of `GET /api/admin/mcp-audit`: the calls, newest first.

admin_console_url.description: `None` in `dev` mode: there is no IdP, so no console.

peers.description: The peer stages `NOVA_PEER_STAGES` configures, so the Deployments page can offer them.

shared_account.description: This sign-in is shared by many people (the public demo); its data is reset nightly.

MetricsResponse.description: `GET /api/catalog/metrics`: what is in each catalog the caller may browse.

catalogs.description:
One entry per catalog the caller may browse: bronze, silver, gold first, then the
rest by name.

generatedAt.description:
When this answer was built (Unix ms). The numbers themselves are from the last
background round, which `updatedAt` on each row names.

totals.description: The sums over `catalogs`, leaving out the `pending` ones.

MetricsTotals.description:
The sums over every catalog in the answer. Pending catalogs contribute nothing: their
zeros are not numbers, and a tile must not read "0 tables" while the scan runs.

catalogs.description: How many catalogs with numbers are listed.

records.description: Rows in the loaded tables' current snapshots.

sizeBytes.description: Bytes the loaded tables' snapshots occupy.

MigrationFile.description: One file, as the bundle has it. The client hashes the bytes it deploys.

name.description: `NNN_<words>.sql`: three digits, an underscore, lower-case words, `.sql`.

sha256.description: The file's sha256, 64 lower-case hex digits.

ModelEndpointRow.description: One endpoint as the UI and Ask need it. No `url`, no `keyRef`.

perGroupMonthlyTokens.description: `spec.quota.perGroupMonthlyTokens`: the tokens one group may spend a month, if set.

perPersonDailyTokens.description: `spec.quota.perPersonDailyTokens`: the tokens one person may spend a day, if set.

sendRows.description: May query results be sent to this model? Off by default.

month.description: `YYYY-MM`, the calendar month the totals cover (UTC).

NamespacesResponse.description: Iceberg `ListNamespaces` result: each namespace is a list of levels.

NewConnection.description:
`POST /api/connections` body. `secret` holds the values; they are written to the store and
never returned.

secret.description: The secret field values. Write-only: Nova stores them and never reads them back.

bundle.description: The bundle that was deployed, 1 to 64 characters, no `/`.

files.description: The files of the bundle this deploy read, at most 200; empty when the caller sent none.

ownerGroup.description: The owner group of the deployed pipelines; the caller must be a member.

pipelines.description: The pipelines the deploy touched, at most 200.

planId.description:
The `planId` of the plan this apply followed (`POST /api/deployments/plan`), or absent. When
given, the row must describe the same rendered set the plan named; otherwise 409.

previousDeploymentId.description:
The deployment a rollback replayed, or absent. It is display metadata: the page links to it, and a row the
caller may not see answers 404 there.

resources.description: The rendered Pipeline documents this deploy applied; empty for a failed deploy.

revision.description: The commit that was deployed, or absent when it is not known.

target.description: The stage the deploy went to, 1 to 64 characters, no `/`.

warehouse.description: The warehouse the query was written for; free text, may be empty.

NewTeam.description:
One `POST /api/admin/teams` body: a new team space.

The group comes from the company's sign-in provider; stardelt never creates groups,
so `group` must already exist there.

description.description: `spec.description` of the production catalog; the other two carry a fixed sentence.

group.description: The group the three catalogs belong to.

team.description: The team's short name: 2 to 21 lower-case letters and digits, starting with a letter.

NewTeamResponse.description: What a created team space answers: its three catalogs and its pipeline principal.

principalCreated.description: False when the principal already existed for another team of the same group.

expected.description: The known answer: up to 100 rows, each an array of values, or absent.

sql.description: One read-only statement, at most 20 000 characters.

default.description:
The default as the cell would run it: a string literal without its quotes, any
other literal exactly as written. Never evaluated.

NotebookParameters.description:
`GET /api/notebooks/{group}/{name}/parameters`: the parameters of one pinned version
(stardelt-nova#237).

objectVersion.description:
The version the answer describes — the one asked for, or the latest when the query
named none. A schedule pins this exact id.

parameters.description:
The `name = literal` lines of the first cell tagged `parameters`, in order, at most
32; empty when no cell carries the tag.

NotebookRequest.description:
The published notebook version a schedule pins (#237): the `.ipynb` file name, the immutable
object version a publish answered, and the parameters the run passes to papermill.

connection.description:
The `Connection` whose secret fields the task pod receives as `CONN_<NAME>_<KEY>`
(the CRD's `tasks[].connection`). Omitted: the pod gets no connection variable. Nova
checks the shape only; whether the connection exists, is Ready, is of this group and is
in its `usableBy` is the loader's job, and its sentence is the one the task log shows.

name.description:
`<group>/<name>` is the object key; the group is the pipeline's `ownerGroup`, so a
notebook of another group can never be named.

objectVersion.description: The S3 object version, never a branch or a tag: exactly the bytes a person published.

params.description:
Parameter values by name; at most 32, names `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}`, values up to
256 characters. Written as the task's `config.params` JSON object string.

NotebookScheduleRow.description:
One pipeline that runs a published notebook (`GET /api/notebooks/{group}/{name}/usage`,
stardelt-nova#517): a Schedule is a one-task `Pipeline` (#516), so this is its resource.

cron.description: `spec.schedule.cron`; `None` for a pipeline that runs on demand.

objectVersion.description: The pinned `config.objectVersion`; a schedule runs exactly these bytes.

timezone.description: `spec.schedule.timezone`; `None` for a pipeline that runs on demand.

NotebookSource.description:
Where a published version came from, as the publisher reported it (stardelt-nova#819).
A claim: Nova stores it and does not check it against a Git server.

clean.description: `false` when the publisher reported uncommitted changes to this file.

path.description: The notebook's path from the repository root.

uploadedAt.description:
The version's `LastModified` as RFC 3339 in UTC (`2026-10-21T01:24:28.000Z`),
whichever of S3's two date shapes the gateway answered.

uploadedBy.description: The `x-amz-meta-uploaded-by` the publisher wrote (their display name).

viewers.description: Groups that may read it without being members.

schedules.description: The visible pipelines that run this notebook, sorted by name.

oneOf.description: Where the version came from; null when the publisher sent no X-Stardelt-Source header.

uploadedAt.description:
The version's `LastModified` as RFC 3339 in UTC (`2026-10-21T01:24:28.000Z`),
whichever of S3's two date shapes the gateway answered.

OidcMe.description:
`/api/me` in `oidc` mode: claims, never tokens. Nova still talks to Trino and
Lakekeeper with its service connection, and says so (`identity_forwarding`).

admin_by.description: `"group"` or `"role"`: which of the two `admin_group` is. `None` with it.

admin_console_url.description: Realm admin console derived from the issuer; `None` for non-Keycloak issuers.

admin_group.description:
The configured value behind this caller's administrator decision: the group
matched, or the role held (and the configured precedence for a member). `None`
when neither is configured (#213).

peers.description: The peer stages `NOVA_PEER_STAGES` configures, so the Deployments page can offer them.

session_expires_at.description:
Unix seconds at which the browser session can no longer be renewed and the
person signs in again; `None` for an Authorization-header call, which has no
session. Never the access token's own `exp`.

shared_account.description: This sign-in is shared by many people (the public demo); its data is reset nightly.

name.description: The name the caller passes as `?peer=`; 1 to 24 lower-case letters, digits and dashes.

url.description: The peer's base URL, without a trailing slash.

airflowUrl.description: The public Airflow DAG URL, `None` when `NOVA_BASE_DOMAIN` is unset; the route is already visibility-gated, so no second permission check.

oneOf.description: Who is told when a run ends; left out when the resource has none.

options.description:
Retries, the wait between them, the time limit and the run mode as the resource carries
them, with the defaults filled in when a field is absent.

PipelineDetail.description:
`GET /api/pipelines/{namespace}/{name}`: the view, the latest runs and the resource's
parameters, retry policy and options.

PipelineDocument.description:
`GET /api/pipelines/{namespace}/{name}/spec`: the editable document of a pipeline, in the shape
of the body of `pipelines_create`, so it can be edited and sent to `pipelines_validate` as it is.

oneOf.description: The pinned notebook of a notebook pipeline.
Who is told when a run ends; left out when the resource has none.

options.description: Retries, the wait, the time limit and the run mode, defaults filled in.

params.description: The values of `${params.<name>}`; left out when there are none.

oneOf.description:
How the writes reach the tables people read (`spec.publish`); left out when the pipeline
writes straight to `main`.
The cron and its zone; a resource without a zone is `UTC`, as the loader reads it.

sql.description: The statement of a statement pipeline.

tasks.description:
The tasks of a task-list pipeline (`sql`, `notebook` and `dbt` tasks), in the shape
`pipelines_validate` accepts; left out for a single-task pipeline.

viewers.description: Groups that may read the pipeline without being members; left out when there are none.

PipelineNotify.description:
Who is told when a run of this pipeline ends (`spec.notify`, operator#582 / nova#815).
Each list names at most five destinations owned by the pipeline's `ownerGroup`.

onFailure.description: Destinations told when the run fails, after the last retry.

onRecovered.description: Destinations told on the first success after a failure.

onSuccess.description: Destinations told when the run succeeds.

PipelineOptions.description:
The advanced options of a schedule (#223), all optional: an omitted field keeps today's
default (one retry, five minutes between retries, a two-hour time limit, one run at a time).
`Replace` is deliberately not offered — the loader treats it as `Forbid`.

backoffMinutes.description: The wait between attempts, 1 to 60 minutes.

concurrency.description: `Forbid` (one run at a time, the default) or `Allow` (runs side by side).

retries.description: Extra attempts after a failure, 0 to 5.

timeoutMinutes.description: The longest a whole run may take, 1 to 720 minutes.

PipelineOptionsView.description: The options as the resource carries them, defaults filled in — what the edit dialog prefills.

editable.description:
True when Nova may change it: Nova wrote it and it has the shape the form edits (one
`run` task, a statement or a notebook) or a task list (every task `sql`, `notebook` or
`dbt`), which an update replaces whole. A pipeline that is not editable is still shown.

managedBy.description: `nova` when Nova wrote the pipeline, `other` for one made with kubectl or by GitOps.

resourceVersion.description: The resource's `resourceVersion`, for a later edit to detect a concurrent change.

PipelineTaskRequest.description:
One task of a task-list body (`#905`): the name the engine uses, exactly one of a statement, a
notebook, a dbt run, a quality run and a spark-pipeline graph, and the tasks that must succeed
first.

oneOf.description: A `dbt` run instead of a statement or a notebook (`#112`): exactly one of the five.

dependsOn.description: Names of the tasks that must succeed first; at most 8, each a task of this list.

name.description: Unique within the pipeline: `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,62}` (the CRD also accepts capitals).

oneOf.description: A published notebook version to run instead (#237).

SQL assertions instead of a statement, a notebook or a dbt run (`#114`): exactly one of
the five.

A declared Spark graph instead of a statement, a notebook, a dbt run or SQL checks
(#80): exactly one of the five.

sql.description:
The statement to run; exactly one of this, `notebook`, `dbt`, `quality` and
`sparkPipeline` is given.

writes.description:
The tables a `spark-pipeline` or `notebook` task writes, as `catalog.schema.table`; at most 16.
`spec.publish: wap` audits exactly these tables (#114).

PipelineView.description: One pipeline in the list: the resource plus what Airflow says about it.

canEdit.description:
Whether the caller may also pause, resume, change or delete it — the owner group and
administrators only (epic#895 decision 12).

canRun.description: Whether the caller may run it and stop its runs.

createdAt.description:
`metadata.creationTimestamp` as the cluster wrote it (RFC 3339); `None` for a malformed
resource.

oneOf.description:
The bundle, target and commit a deploy stamped on the pipeline; absent for one that was
made in the interface or with `stardelt apply`.

description.description: `spec.description`: one line about what the pipeline does; absent for most.

loaded.description: `false` while Airflow has no DAG for the resource yet; the loader needs about 25 seconds.

publish.description:
`spec.publish`: `direct` (the default) or `wap` — a `wap` run writes an audit
branch, runs its checks, and only a passing run publishes (#114).

schedule.description: The cron schedule, with the time zone in parentheses when there is one.

state.description:
`loading`, `paused`, `running`, `failed`, `succeeded`, `idle`, or `not-loaded` after three
minutes without a DAG.

approvable.description: Whether this Nova can record an approval (a state store is configured).

errors.description: One sentence per problem: a changed file, a file added before an applied one.

ledger.description: Whether `stardelt_meta.migrations` exists in the catalog yet (false on a fresh catalog).

ok.description: False when `errors` is not empty: the bundle must not be applied as it is.

planId.description: The identity of this plan: what `bundle approve` takes and what apply needs.

action.description:
`create`, `update`, `unchanged` or `delete` (from `ValidatePipelineResponse::action`, with
`create` when `action` is absent). A `delete` is a pipeline this bundle and target own that
the set omits, present only when `prune` is true, and it carries no `diff`.

diff.description: What an `update` would change, the sentences `pipelines_validate` answers.

new.description:
`true` when the newest applied deployment of this bundle and target does not name this path
with this digest; every file when no deployment was recorded yet.

message.description: One sentence, the same sentence the write route would refuse with.

path.description: Where the problem is: `resources[2] (gold)` or `resources` (the set).

catalog.description: The catalog the sink tables live in; the ledger is `stardelt_meta` in it.

files.description: Every migration file of the bundle, in any order; the answer sorts them by name.

target.description: The bundle target whose ledger rows count (`dev`, `prod`, …).

class.description: `additive` when every statement only adds (see `classify`), else `breaking`.

reason.description: The first statement that is not additive, cut to 120 characters. Absent for `additive`.

statements.description: How many statements the file holds, as the splitter counts them.

status.description: `new` (not in the ledger), `applied` (same sha) or `changed` (applied with another sha).

browsable.description:
Whether a browser has somewhere to go for this app. False for an app with
no browsable surface of its own (an API-only catalog, say), which is
independent of whether the app is installed or reachable.

external_url.description:
Reachable-from-the-browser URL. Empty when no base domain is configured,
and empty for an app with no browsable surface (nothing serves its host —
see `public_url`).

images.description:
Images the app's workloads actually run, read from the cluster. Empty when
there is no cluster to read (demo mode, local run) or the app is not installed.

PreviewScheduleRequest.description: `POST /api/pipelines/preview-schedule`: the next fire times of a cron in its zone.

count.description: How many runs to list, 1 to 10; 5 when omitted.

runs.description: The next fire times in the schedule's zone, RFC 3339 with that offset.

PrincipalView.description: One of the caller's groups and its pipeline principal.

message.description:
`null` when ready; otherwise the `Ready` condition's message, or `no status yet`, or the
`make sync-principal` command for a group without a principal.

principal.description: `pipeline-<group>` when such a `ServicePrincipal` of this group exists.

Provenance.description:
Where a pipeline came from when `stardelt bundle deploy` published it. It names things and
decides nothing: it is shown on the pipeline page and lets a later deploy find what a bundle
owns. Written as the labels `stardelt.io/bundle` and `stardelt.io/target` and the annotation
`stardelt.io/revision`, plus who deployed and when.

bundle.description: The bundle's name: 3 to 40 lower-case letters, digits and dashes.

repository.description:
The bundle's repository as an `https://host/path` address, so a later stage can link the
pull request that promotes a commit. Omitted when the bundle's checkout names none.

revision.description:
The commit the bundle was read at: 7 to 64 hex digits, with `-dirty` appended when the
working tree had uncommitted changes. Omitted when the bundle is not in a Git checkout.

target.description: The target of the bundle: 1 to 32 lower-case letters, digits and dashes.

Publish.description:
How a pipeline's writes reach the tables people read: straight to `main`, or through an
audit branch that a `quality` task must pass first (`spec.publish`, #114).

objectVersion.description: The immutable S3 version id a schedule pins.

sha256.description: Lower-case hex SHA-256 of the stored bytes (outputs already stripped).

oneOf.description: Where the version came from; null when the publisher sent no X-Stardelt-Source header.

unchanged.description:
`true` when the newest version already holds these exact bytes: nothing was stored and
`objectVersion` is that version.

QualityCheckRequest.description:
One SQL assertion of a `quality` task (`#114`): a name the task log shows, the statement that
must return no rows, and how a non-empty answer is treated.

severity.description: `error` fails the run, `warn` only logs it; omitted is `error`.

sql.description: The assertion: it passes when the query returns no rows.

QualityRequest.description:
A `quality` task of a task list (`#114`): SQL assertions the loader runs after the task's
predecessors. The rules are `demos/dags/stardelt_pipelines/plan.py`'s, so Nova refuses what the
loader would refuse.

checks.description: 1 to 50 SQL assertions; a check passes when its query returns no rows.

QueryData.description: How much data the query read, wrote and held in memory.

QueryHistory.description: The runs of the same statement that the caller can see, newest first.

medianWallMs.description: Median wall time of `runs` in milliseconds; null when no run has a timing.

slower.description: True when this query's wall time is more than twice the median and at least three runs were compared.

QueryLogDetail.description: Everything stored about one query: the whole statement, timing, data volumes, tables.

user.description: The raw engine user (the `sub` once authz 8/8 is live).

QueryLogItem.description: One row of the query log list; the statement is cut to a preview.

user.description: The raw engine user (the `sub` once authz 8/8 is live).

userName.description:
The person's display name when Nova knows the engine user; `None` falls back to
`user` in the UI.

QueryLogPage.description: One page of the query log; `nextCursor` is null on the last page.

sql.description: One SQL statement, run with the caller's identity.

rows.description: One array per row, in column order; values are JSON scalars, arrays or objects.

stats.description: The engine's statistics object, passed through unchanged.

truncated.description:
True when rows were cut at [`MAX_ROWS`] or [`MAX_BYTES`]: the result is a prefix, not the
whole answer. The UI says so instead of showing a silent partial table.

QueryTiming.description: How long the query waited, planned and ran, in milliseconds.

ReadTable.description: One table a person read most, with its newest write.

lastWrite.description: The newest write in the window; absent when nothing wrote it.

namespace.description: `<catalog>.<schema>` (demo data may carry the schema alone).

queries.description: Read-only queries against it in the window.

RefreshAccepted.description:
The answer to an accepted `POST /api/catalog/metrics/refresh`: the round runs in the
background, and the page reads the new numbers with its next request.

accepted.description: Always `true`: a `202` is the acceptance, and the round has already started.

RetriesView.description: The retry policy of a pipeline.

snapshot_id.description:
The snapshot to return to, as a string of digits (an Iceberg id has 64 bits; a JSON
number is accepted too but a browser rounds it).

RotateRequest.description:
`PUT …/secret` body: the field values to write. Write-only, like the create body, and never
printed — no `Debug` on purpose.

secret.description: The fields to rotate; a managed connection sends every field.

RunQueryView.description: One statement a run's task sent to the engine (nova#788 S5).

sql.description: The statement; string literals are replaced by `?` under NOVA_QUERY_LOG_REDACT_LITERALS=1.

taskId.description: The task id from the `task=` client tag, when the loader sent one.

RunResponse.description: `GET …/runs/{run_id}`: one run and its task instances.

RunStart.description: The body of `POST …/runs`: a run date and parameter values for this run only (nova#817).

RunView.description: One DagRun. `type` is Airflow's `run_type` under the name the UI uses.

bundle.description: The bundle the run's pipeline was deployed from, when it came from one.

revision.description: The Git revision that deployment named; absent for a dirty tree.

groups.description:
Every owner group of a pipeline the caller can see, sorted; the runs filters do not
narrow it. Administrators (`ownerGroup: null`) are not a group.

RunsListRow.description: One run in the cross-pipeline list (`GET /api/runs`).

SavedQuery.description: A row as the API returns it. Times are epoch milliseconds, like `Job.started_at`.

ScheduleRequest.description: A cron expression and its IANA zone; both required when a `schedule` object is sent.

matches.description: Matches in order of namespace, then table.

truncated.description:
True when more tables match than were returned, or when the catalog has more namespaces than one
request reads (100): the answer is then a prefix, so narrow the words or name the catalog.

message.description: `null` when ready; otherwise the same sentence the Schedule dialog would refuse with.

ServicePrincipalsResponse.description: `GET /api/service-principals`: the principals the caller may see.

Snapshot.description:
What Nova knows about the namespace, and how it knows it.

The list alone is not enough: an empty list means "nothing is there" *or* "the cluster
did not answer", and those are very different things to show a person. `error` plus
`age_seconds` (time since the last successful read) let the UI say which.

age_seconds.description: Seconds since the last successful read. `None` when there never was one.

error.description:
Set when the most recent read failed; the workloads above are then the last known
good state, not the current one.

state.description:
`ok` | `stale` | `unreachable` — computed here rather than by the client, so the
UI and the API cannot disagree about what an empty list means.

SparkPipelineRequest.description:
A `spark-pipeline` task of a task list (#80): the declared graph `spark-pipelines` runs on
the owner group's `SparkCluster`. `project` is a directory of the bundle.

fullRefresh.description: Datasets to rebuild from scratch; 1 to 32 names.

SqlWarehouse.description: One warehouse a caller may use, as the UI shows it.

canUse.description:
One of the caller's groups is granted this class (`spec.grants`). Non-authoritative:
the engine decides, this only fails before the person tries.

default.description: `spec.default`: the class a query lands in when no selector matches.

displayName.description:
`spec.displayName`, or `null` when the object carries none. The UI falls back to
`name`; Nova never invents a label.

memoryShare.description: Share of the engine's memory the class may use, for example `20%`.

name.description: `metadata.name`: the `SqlWarehouse` object, and the `wh-<name>` resource group.

queued.description: Queries that may wait (the resource group's queue limit).

running.description: Queries that run at the same time (the resource group's hard concurrency limit).

oneOf.description: The scaler's verdict on the engine (`status.scale`); `None` before it has one.

size.description:
`spec.size` (`xs`, `small`, `medium`, `large`). `null` for the synthetic administrator
row, which is not a class of its own.

yours.description: The row this caller will land in: the largest usable class, or the default one.

detail.description: One sentence for the page when `status` is not `ok`; absent otherwise.

there.description: The peer's, empty when `status` is not `ok`.

StageRow.description: One deployed pipeline of a stage, as the comparison needs it.

repository.description: The bundle's repository, so the page can link the pull request that promotes a commit.

idleSeconds.description: Seconds since the last request that named this statement; Nova forgets it an hour after that.

statementId.description: The handle for every other call.

truncated.description: True when the rows were cut (see `statements_get`).

StatementView.description: A statement as the caller sees it.

chunks.description: Chunks readable now: every full chunk while the statement runs, the last partial one too once it ends.

columns.description: Known once the engine has sent them; empty before.

error.description: The engine's one-line reason when `state` is `FAILED` or `CANCELED`.

rows.description: Chunk 0 when `state` is `SUCCEEDED`, so a short statement needs one call; absent otherwise.

statementId.description: The engine's query id; the handle for every other call.

truncated.description: True when the rows were cut (at 100 000 rows or at about 64 MiB of data): they are a prefix, not the whole answer.

StoredSetting.description: What `PUT /api/settings/{key}` answers: the key and the value as stored.

connectionRef.description: Name of the `Connection` (`type: kafka`); absent means the platform's own bus.

StreamState.description: The one verb a stream has: stop or resume by setting `spec.stopped`.

StreamView.description: One `StreamApp`, as the Streams page needs it. No secret, no checkpoint path.

attempts.description:
How many times Spark has submitted the application (`status.attempts`); absent until
the operator reports it (operator#336).

oneOf.description:
What a bundle deploy stamped on the stream: bundle, target, revision, repository,
who and when. Absent when no bundle wrote it. `modified` is true when the spec was
changed after the last deploy.

last_submitted_at.description: When Spark last submitted the application, RFC 3339 (`status.lastSubmittedAt`).

reason.description: The `Ready` condition's reason, when the operator set one (operator#322: `Restarting`).

viewers.description: The groups that may read the stream without being members (`spec.viewers`).

StreamWrite.description:
The body of a stream write (`nova#617` slice a). No credentials: `connectionRef` is the
name of a `Connection`, and Nova never stores or forwards a secret.

name.description: The stream's name; the `PUT` path is authoritative and a different body name is refused.

ownerGroup.description: The group that owns the stream; the caller must be a member.

oneOf.description:
Which bundle, target and commit this write deploys (`stardelt bundle deploy`).
Omitted leaves what the stream already carries untouched.

viewers.description:
Groups that may read this stream without being members (`spec.viewers`), read-only.
At most 16, each a group name; empty writes none.

namespace.description: Nova's own namespace: every stream lives here, and a write's path names it.

maxRows.description:
The most rows to keep, 1 to 100 000 (the default and the cap). A longer result is cut here, the query
is cancelled in the engine and the statement ends `SUCCEEDED` with `truncated: true`.

sql.description: One SQL statement, run with the caller's identity.

waitSeconds.description: How long the call waits for the statement to end before it answers `202`; 0 to 30, default 5.

TableDocumentation.description: The documentation of one table, plus what the caller may do with it.

canEdit.description: Whether the interim rule lets this caller edit (see the module docs).

canRollback.description: Whether this caller may roll the table back (catalog owner group or administrator).

columns.description: The fields of the **current** schema, in schema order.

editRule.description: One sentence for a person: why `canEdit` has the value it has.

guide.description: The `stardelt.guide` property: how to use this table (joins, filters, definitions), or `null`.

owner.description: The `stardelt.owner` property: a group name, or `null`.

rollbackRule.description: One sentence for a person: why `canRollback` has the value it has.

tags.description: The `stardelt.tags` property, split on commas, trimmed and sorted.

TableIdentifier.description: One Iceberg object identifier: a table or a view.

kind.description:
`table` or `view`. Iceberg REST lists them through two endpoints; the explorer needs to
tell them apart, and only a table has `/tables/{ns}/{tbl}` metadata.

TableMetadataResponse.description:
Iceberg `LoadTable` result: where the metadata lives plus the metadata
document itself (schema, partition specs, properties). The metadata body
is the catalog's own document — Nova never reshapes it.

TaskSpecView.description:
One task as the resource declares it. A `sql` task's statement and a `notebook` task's file
name, version and parameters are carried only by the detail route (Schedule's edit dialog
prefills from them).

connection.description:
The `Connection` a `kind: "notebook"` task names (`tasks[].connection`), detail route
only. Shape-checked by Nova; the loader decides whether the task may use it.

dbtProject.description: The project of a `kind: "dbt"` task (`config.project`), detail route only.

dbtSelect.description: The selector or the batched selectors, joined with `, `, detail route only.

dependsOn.description: The task names this task waits for (`tasks[].dependsOn`).

fullRefresh.description: The datasets a full refresh rebuilds, detail route only.

notebook.description: The `.ipynb` file name of a `kind: "notebook"` task (#237).

notebookParams.description: The parameters a notebook task passes, parsed back from `config.params`.

objectVersion.description: The immutable object version a notebook task pins.

project.description: The bundle directory of a `kind: "spark-pipeline"` task, detail route only.

refresh.description: `incremental` or `full` of a `kind: "spark-pipeline"` task, detail route only.

writes.description:
`tasks[].writes` (`catalog.schema.table`), detail route only (#114): the tables a
`wap` run audits.

TaskView.description: One task instance of a run.

UpdatePipelineRequest.description:
`PUT /api/pipelines/{namespace}/{name}`: change the statement, the schedule, the parameters
and the options — or, for a notebook pipeline, the notebook, its version and its parameters.
Every other field of the resource stays as it is, and what the pipeline runs never changes
kind.

oneOf.description:
The notebook, its version and its parameters for a notebook pipeline; a statement
pipeline refuses it.
The whole option set; omitted means the defaults.

params.description: The whole parameter table; omitted means none.

oneOf.description:
Which bundle, target and commit this update deploys. Omitted leaves what the pipeline
already says untouched; given, it replaces it.

How the writes reach the tables people read (`spec.publish`, #114). Omitted on a create
means `direct`; on an update it keeps what the pipeline says, and `direct` removes it.

resourceVersion.description:
The `resourceVersion` the caller read (`pipelines_spec`). When it is given and is not the
stored one, somebody changed the pipeline in between: 409 `the pipeline changed while you
edited it: reload`, and nothing is written. Omitted keeps the old behaviour (the update
then only fails if the resource changes while the update itself runs).

oneOf.description: Omitted means no schedule: the pipeline then runs on demand only.

sql.description: The statement of a statement pipeline; a notebook pipeline refuses it.

tasks.description:
A whole task list instead of one `run` task (`#905`): 1 to 30 tasks, each a statement, a
pinned notebook, a dbt run or SQL checks, with dependencies. Exclusive with `sql` and
`notebook`.

viewers.description: Omitted keeps the stored viewers; an empty list removes them.

UsagePage.description: Compute and bytes added up, with the window that was used.

from.description: The window that was added up, epoch milliseconds.

total.description: Every item added together; its `key` is `total`.

UsageRow.description: The month's tokens, per group and endpoint.

estimatedCalls.description: Calls whose token counts were estimated (`ceil(bytes / 4)`), so the page can say "about".

group.description: The group, or `(none)` for `nova`'s probe rows and callers without a group.

ValidatePipelineResponse.description: `POST /api/pipelines/validate`: what a create (or an apply) of this document would do, without doing it.

action.description:
`create` when the name is free, `update` when it names a pipeline Nova wrote and the caller
may change; absent when `ok` is false.

changes.description:
What an `update` would change, from `statement` (or `notebook`), `schedule`, `params` and
`options`; empty for a `create`, for a refusal and for an update that changes nothing.

errors.description: Why not: one sentence per problem (today the first rule that refuses).

modified.description:
`true` for an `update` of a pipeline that was changed after its last deploy
(`deployment.modified` of the pipeline view): applying this document overwrites that
change. Absent otherwise.

nextRuns.description:
The next five fire times (RFC 3339, in the schedule's zone) when the document is accepted
and has a schedule.

ok.description: True when the document would be accepted.

VerifiedQuery.description: A row as the API returns it. `verified_at` and `last_check_at` are RFC 3339 in UTC.

expected.description: The expected result: one array per row, each holding the row's values, or `null`.

lastCheckAt.description: When the query was last checked, RFC 3339, or `null` when it never was.

lastCheckMessage.description: What the last check found, in one sentence, or `null` when it never ran.

lastCheckPassed.description: Whether the last check passed, or `null` when it never ran.

question.description: The question a person asks, in words.

sql.description: The one read-only statement that answers it.

verifiedBy.description: The `sub` of the person who verified it.

WarehouseInfo.description:
OpenAPI shapes for the catalog routes (first slice of ticket #107).

Nova proxies these bodies — from Lakekeeper upstream, or from the
in-memory demo shapes in `demo.rs` — so the structs below mirror the
proxied Iceberg REST shapes rather than being constructed anywhere.
`#[schema(rename = …)]` keeps the hyphenated Iceberg field names.

id.description: The Lakekeeper warehouse id, or `"demo"` in demo mode.

WarehouseScale.description:
What the engine is doing for one class: `status.scale`, which the platform's access-sync job
writes (`patch_scale_status`) and Nova only reads. `None` until the scaler has reached the
object, or without a cluster.

lastQueryAt.description:
The last completed query's end, RFC 3339 (`stardelt.io/last-query-at`); `null` while the
class has no measurement.

queriesInFlight.description: Queries the class reported as running at its last report (`stardelt.io/queries-in-flight`).

workers.description:
Worker replicas the scaler last set for the one engine every class shares, so every row of
one answer carries the same number.

WarehouseStart.description:
The answer to `POST /api/warehouses/{name}/start`: the class, and the phase the scaler will
report once it has woken the engine. Nova never writes `status` — 202 is the whole promise.

Workload.description: One workload in the namespace, flattened to what a human wants to see.

image.description: Image reference as the cluster has it — tag or digest, verbatim.

WorkspaceView.description:
One workspace as the card shows it. `state` is one of `stopped`, `starting`, `running`,
`stopping` and `unavailable`; the three times are RFC 3339 in UTC, or `null` while the hub
reports none.

idleStopAt.description: `last_activity` plus `NOVA_WORKSPACE_IDLE_SECONDS`: when the hub culls an idle server.

bearer.description: An access token from the platform's identity provider, sent in the `Authorization` header. In `dev` mode no credential is needed.

session.name: nova_session
session.description: The signed session cookie the browser sign-in sets. Same rules as the bearer token.

tags.name: public
tags.description: Stable surface for tools and scripts. Breaking changes bump `info.version`.

tags.name: internal
tags.description: UI-only surface. May change or disappear without notice; do not build tools on it.
